entry.title: I Finally Understand .gitkeep
entry.summary:
You may have often come across a .gitkeep file in a Git repository. Have you ever wondered what it's actually for? After doing some research, I finally realized that .gitkeep is not an official Git feature or standard like .gitignore. .gitkeep Used For?
By default, Git doesn't track empty directories. This means if you create a folder without any files inside, Git will ignore it. That's where .gitkeep comes in. It's simply a placeholder file added to an empty directory so Git can include the folder in version control. By placing a file like .gitkeep in an otherwise empty directory, Git will recognize that the directory is part of the repository. A common example is an uploads directory. This folder is often empty in the repository but required by the application to store uploaded files. Even though it starts out empty, the directory must exist so the application can run properly. That's why a .gitkeep file is used to ensure the folder is tracked by Git. It's important to note that .gitkeep is not a Git-specific file. You can use any filename like .keep, README.md or even .gitignore as long it ensures the directory is no longer empty. The most important is, there must be at least one file in the directory, so Git can track it. .gitkeep is simply an unofficial convention used to keep empty directories in Git repositories. Git itself doesn't care about the file name, as long as the directory isn't empty, it will be tracked.

entry.summary: A business transaction ideally involves a single roundtrip to the database. MongoDB allows a single document to hold all transaction data, simplifying sharding and scaling. This results in higher latency when the application is closer to the user and farther from the database.
